Symptom: Endpoint latency grows linearly with collection size; many tiny SELECTs in trace
Fix: Eager-load (JOIN / prefetch_related / Include); batch IDs; use DataLoader for GraphQL
Keywords: n+1 query orm lazy load dataloader
Notes: Classic. DataLoader pattern (Facebook) is the standard fix for GraphQL resolvers.

Symptom: Slow query, high CPU on DB
Fix: Add the right index (covering / partial / expression); reorganise query
Notes: Use 'EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)' on Postgres; aim for 'Index Scan' on hot paths.

Symptom: Same query suddenly slow after data growth
Fix: ANALYZE; raise statistics target; pg_hint_plan or rewrite; partition
Notes: Set 'auto_explain' on slow queries in prod for evidence.

Symptom: Tail latency spikes, 'too many connections' errors
Root Cause: Pool too big or too small; per-pod pool > DB max
Fix: Use a proxy pool (PgBouncer); pool_size_per_pod = (db_max - margin)/total_pods; transaction-pooling mode
Notes: Postgres can handle ~200-500 active connections; for thousands of clients use PgBouncer transaction pooling.

Symptom: Periodic latency spikes correlated with allocation
Root Cause: Allocation rate too high; old-gen survivors
Fix: Profile allocations; use object pooling sparingly; tune GC (G1 → ZGC/Shenandoah on JVM)
Keywords: gc pause zgc shenandoah pprof async-profiler
Notes: JVM 17+ ZGC keeps pauses sub-millisecond; Go GC pauses are usually negligible — investigate allocation rate instead.

Fix: Re-hash / salt the key; client-side caching for read; isolate hot tenant
Keywords: hot key skew partition kafka redis
Notes: Add a small random suffix (key+'#'+rand(0..9)) for hot read keys; multi-key lookup.

Root Cause: Slow replicas, GC, JIT warmup, network jitter
Fix: Hedged requests, request coalescing, JIT warm-up, profile slow path
Keywords: tail latency p99 hedged dean barroso
Notes: See 'The Tail at Scale'. Beware single-replica 'fan-out' calls.

Symptom: Cold cache → all clients hit origin simultaneously
Fix: Single-flight loader / request coalescing; jittered TTLs; warm cache
Keywords: thundering herd cache stampede single flight
Notes: Add small random TTL jitter; coalesce concurrent loads per key.

Symptom: Latency rises under load even with async code
Root Cause: Blocking IO/CPU work on event loop / async runtime
Fix: Move to dedicated worker pool; use async drivers; offload CPU to threads
Keywords: async block event loop tokio asyncio
Notes: Don't call sync DB drivers from async code; tokio-console diagnoses task starvation in Rust.

Root Cause: Cold container init, large bundle, JVM warmup
Fix: Use SnapStart (Java); provisioned concurrency; trim deps; native AOT
Keywords: cold start lambda snapstart provisioned concurrency
Notes: SnapStart cuts JVM cold starts ~10×; native-image (GraalVM) gives Go-class startup.

Root Cause: Unreleased references; growing caches; goroutine/thread leaks
Fix: Heap dumps; bounded caches; close clients; cancellation contexts everywhere
Tooling: jcmd / heapdump, pprof heap, clinic.js, valgrind massif
Keywords: memory leak heap pprof jcmd valgrind
Notes: Bound every cache (size + TTL); always pass 'context.Context' / 'CancellationToken'.

Symptom: Goroutine count grows; CPU stable, latency degrades
Root Cause: Forgotten 'go' calls without ctx; channels never closed
Fix: Always pass context; close channels deterministically; tokio JoinSet/Tower budget
Notes: Inspect 'pprof?goroutine' periodically in canary; alert on sustained growth.

Root Cause: Unclosed clients / responses; ulimit too low
Fix: Defer Close everywhere; share clients (DON'T create per-request); raise ulimit / nofile
Notes: Java/Node/Go HTTP clients should be singletons (with connection pool), never per-request.

Root Cause: Per-request allocations in hot path (boxing, string concat)
Fix: Reuse buffers (sync.Pool / ArrayPool); switch to streaming JSON; avoid reflection
Notes: On Go: 'GODEBUG=allocfreetrace' for hot allocs. JVM: async-profiler '--alloc'.

Fix: Use code-gen serializers (jsoniter / sonic / Jackson AfterBurner / System.Text.Json source-gen); switch to Protobuf
Notes: On .NET 8 source-gen serializers ~2× faster than reflection.

Fix: Batch endpoints; combine reads (DataLoader / GraphQL); reduce client→service hops
Notes: Always look at trace waterfall — fix shape of API, not just speed of each hop.

Symptom: High CPU + latency on cold clients
Fix: Enable HTTP keep-alive; HTTP/2 multiplex; session resumption (TLS 1.3 0-RTT)
Notes: Most HTTP clients enable keepalive — check if a proxy in between drops it.
